pages.title: Nice to meet you · Quem é você?
pages.pt: Apresentar-se com I'm: nome, origem e como você está

situation.text: Hoje você conhece Omar, de Austin. Conhecendo uma vizinha: nome e origem.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende a se apresentar como o Paddington: I'm + nome, origem e sentimento.
pages.think: Conhecendo uma vizinha: nome e origem.

pages.hook: In the USA, people often meet neighbors in the hallway or the elevator. A small hello and your name can start a new friendship.

mythfact.s: In the USA, people usually shake hands or wave when they meet for the first time.
mythfact.why: A handshake, a wave or just “Hi!” is common. A kiss on the cheek is not usual.

mythfact.s: Austin is the capital of Texas.
mythfact.why: Austin is the capital city of the state of Texas.

mythfact.s: “How’s it going?” always needs a very long answer.
mythfact.why: It is a greeting. A short answer like “Good, thanks. You?” is perfect.

mythfact.s: You must say your full name and your job in the first minute.
mythfact.why: A first name is enough: “Hi, I’m Daniel.”

mythfact.s: The bear in “A Bear Called Paddington” comes from Peru.
mythfact.why: In the book by Michael Bond (1958), Paddington travels from “darkest Peru” to London.

compare.br: In Brazil, people often greet with a kiss on the cheek or a hug, and talk a lot with neighbors, even on the first day.
compare.us: In the USA, a smile, “Hi” and a small wave are enough. People are friendly, but they also like some space.
compare.tip: Say your name first, then “Nice to meet you.” Short is good.
compare.ask: Introduce yourself in English: your name, your city and your country.

pages.polite: Smile, say your **name**, and add **nice to meet you**. “Welcome!” is what neighbors say to new people.

pages.title: Reading quest — A bear and a new neighbor
text: Maya is new in the building. She lives in **4B**, in Austin, Texas. Today she meets a neighbor in the hallway. He smiles and says, “**Hi! I’m Omar.**”

“Hi, Omar! **Nice to meet you**,” says Maya. “**Nice to meet you too!** **Where are you from?**” Omar asks. “**I’m from** Brazil,” says Maya. “And you?” “**I’m from** Austin,” he says. “**Welcome to the building!**”

Maya thinks about a little bear. In an English book, a family finds a bear at a train station in London. The bear is from Peru. He has a label on his coat: “Please look after this bear.” He is lost and tired, but he is also polite. The family asks his name. “I’m Paddington,” he says. The book is from 1958, and Michael Bond wrote it.
Maya says, “I’m a little like Paddington. I’m new, I’m a long way from home, and I’m looking for friends.” Omar laughs. “**Do you like tacos?**” he asks. “**Yes, I do!** I love tacos,” says Maya.

In Austin, many people eat tacos for breakfast or lunch. Omar says, “There is a good taco place near here. **See you around, neighbor!**” Maya feels happy. Her first day in the new building is not lonely any more.
